body:
CANONICAL: day-to-day landing practice in Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, consolidating 9 earlier notes). These are coordinator practices and lessons, not Greg's words unless quoted; they add no gate or authority beyond the checked-in rules.

WORKTREES. Put parallel worktrees at .worktrees/NAME inside the checkout (ignored by Git); TermAl refuses reviewer delegations outside the project. Build each worktree in its own target/ (leave CARGO_TARGET_DIR unset). Scratch of every kind goes under target/ of the tree you work in; create no other new folder in the main root, since an unignored folder drifts the review freeze and voids a running gate. A gate on one worktree never covers another: after moving a patch onto a new master (saved patch, fast-forward only, never a rebase without Greg's word), run the checks its file types need on that tree and freeze it again. After a changeset lands and done is sealed, the lander runs `cargo clean -q` in that worktree (each one holds 7-15 GB; the disk filled on 2026-10-01). Clean only your own. Never `git worktree remove` while any item still cites its runs: review-runs live under .git/worktrees/NAME and go with it. Record the numbers an evaluator needs in a note, so evidence outlives a run directory.

LANDING ORDER. Engram lands one changeset at a time: the implementer asks Engram::Fable for a landing window, and Fable grants them in turn; others hold their pushes until the holder reports "landed" or the window expires (about 20-30 minutes). When master moves under a ready round, the round is redone on the new master. Request the independent acceptance evaluation on the frozen, gated tree BEFORE the push, and push only after it passes (w-cb353c060502 once passed gate and pair, then failed 0 of 3 after the push). Before evaluation, post a criterion-to-evidence map that claims no more than the tests show.

GATES. Stop or discard a running gate before editing its input, even a gate already moot. Fix-round step 1, before opening any file: for a detached launcher run, end its executor's process tree (the pid from the launch output, after confirming its command line names the run; PowerShell taskkill /T /F /PID N), run `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs recover RUN_DIR`, then edit and freeze again. A gate failure is classified (test or environment defect, product defect) and acted on in the same session; never normalise a retry.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA must be provable from what the independent evaluator can read: the repository at the evaluated source, the item's own holder notes and typed evidence, and the host brief. Not from project memory, another item, a non-holder's note or anything that needs tracker reads (the evaluator brief forbids them). Housekeeping such as revising a memory belongs in notes, not criteria; if a criterion must concern tracker state, the holder quotes the output in a holder note. Revisit when TermAl w-67e7b8bdcade lets the brief carry named memories.

HOST-OBSERVED TESTS. A note, update or gate given another held item's ref moves the session's focus to that item, and the next turn is bound to it. Claim (focus) the item as the LAST work mutation of a turn, run the plain test in the next turn in that item's named source root, and check the store after that turn ends.

TOOLS. In the PowerShell tool, give .NET file APIs ([IO.File]::ReadAllText/WriteAllText) absolute paths: Set-Location doesn't change the directory .NET resolves against (an edit once landed in the main checkout instead of the worktree). Prefer the Edit and Write tools.

INSTALL NOTICE TO TERMAL (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, after Engram::Advisor #897: Termal::Codex correctly stopped a final live proof when its pinned engram.exe hash no longer matched the installed binary). Every landing installs a new binary, even a docs-only one, because the revision is embedded. After verifying each landing, Engram::Fable sends Termal::Fable2 one line with the commit, the full build_fingerprint, the installed exe sha256 (sha256sum C:\Users\grzeg\.cargo\bin\engram.exe) and whether the behaviour changed. A cross-project handoff that needs an exact producer names that installed sha256 and build. When a TermAl live check is pinned, warn it before the next Engram landing.

MEASUREMENTS PIN A COPY (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03, after Engram::Coder's root-cost batch on w-f2f02f2f4024 stopped when Opus's landing moved the installed engram.exe at about 09:38Z). A timing or behaviour measurement that must name its producer copies the installed executable ONCE into its own worktree's target/, records the copy's sha256 equal to the installed one at copy time and its readiness build_fingerprint, and uses that copy for every sample. The installed binary before and after is context only, and producers are never blended. TermAl's live checks already pin a verified copy the same way. Before granting a landing window while a measurement is running, the coordinator warns the measurer.

DISK FULL AGAIN, AND A COORDINATOR SWEEP (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03 about 16:16Z, after Engram::Opus #1182: drive C at 0 bytes free at about 16:10Z, with "no space on device" in a cargo build). An implementer still never cleans another session's worktree. The coordinator may remove target/debug, which is regenerable build output only, from STALE worktrees: no build for many hours and no active owner. It first checks that each absolute path lies inside the repository and ends in .worktrees/NAME/target/debug. Source (even dirty), target/tmp scratch and .git/worktrees/NAME/review-runs stay. That sweep freed 29 GB, from quiet-revision-mismatch, machine-blueprint, named-root-freshness, memory-lifecycle and size-closures-coder. About 97 worktrees exist. When free space on C falls below about 20 GB, sweep stale ones before granting a landing window. Failures during a disk-full period are environment defects: record them once and redo the step.
